transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alexi Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Leah Huang (CTO Tessera), Mateo Rivera (Head of ML), Priya Nair (Procurement)
Links shared: pilot-deck (redwood.com/pilot-deck), security brief (redwood.com/sec-one-pager)

Summary: quick intake focused on per-token unit economics, where Tessera's budget ceiling is ~ $25k/mo for initial production, interest in a phased pilot (hosted -> dedicated) and strict residency/KMS needs for PII.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alexi: hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Leah: yeah, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:09] Alexi: great. Quick intro from our side — im Alexi, i run AE for retail vertical, and samir and jules are going to cover the performance/cost bits.
[00:16] Samir: hi all, samir here, i focus on inference ops, batching, cache and quantization tradeoffs.
[00:22] Leah: thanks. For context, Tessera is building in-app shopping assistant and dynamic merchandising rules, so per-call latency target is ~120 to 200ms P95, and our monthly token budget for phase one is around twenty five k USD.
[00:40] Mateo: to add, we expect 2M tokens/mo initially with spikes during promotions. Currently running a small in-house LLM on a single A100 node, cost is opaque and tail latency is painful.
[00:54] Alexi: ok that helps, so rough constraints: 120-200ms P95, 2M tokens baseline, $25k/mo cap, and data residency — can you confirm that tessera requires keys in their cloud KMS?
[01:08] Leah: yes KMS is mandatory, and PII must not leave region. So private or dedicated preferred if pilot goes beyond eval.
[01:16] Samir: noted. On the econ side we usually break costs into model compute per-token, infra overhead (instances/idle), and fixed platform fees. For hosted we typically show per-token rates with a small networking premium; for dedicated we show reserved cost + commit, with lower per-token compute.
[01:34] Mateo: can you give a ballpark? we understand ranges but want realistic numbers for 2M tokens.
[01:40] Alexi: sure, ballpark: hosted with a mid-size Llama2-ish open model is around $0.0008 to $0.0012 per token depending on batching. Dedicated reserved for an instance pool might amortize to $0.00045-$0.0007 per token at steady state — but that assumes good batching and prefix cache hit rates.
[02:02] Leah: aaa, okay. how big an effect is batching? we can't always batch during interactive sessions.
[02:07] Samir: good question. Batching mostly helps throughput workloads. For chat-style interactive, continuous batching and micro-batching can still help 10-40% depending on inter-arrival. Also prefix (KV) caching for repeated prompts or common system prompts can drop token compute by 20-60% depending on reuse.
[02:26] Mateo: hmm, so for our shopping assistant, lots of repeated system prompts and product data, so cache hit could be decent. but if shoppers type long context or custom prompts, does cache still help?
[02:37] Samir: it depends. If you canonicalize system prompts and product snippets, those are high hit. Free-form user text won't. We recommend a small preprocessor to normalize product attributes — that lifts cache hit substantially.
[02:50] Jules: also quantization: running int8 / q4 variants reduces GPU memory and raises throughput. Some model variants trade slight quality for 30-50% perf wins.
[03:01] Leah: any quality regressions you've seen with q4 for retrieval-augmented generation?
[03:06] Samir: usually minimal for retrieval contexts — the big regressions show on instruction-heavy or long-coherence tasks. We can run evals on your prompt set to confirm.
[03:15] Mateo: timeline — we'd like a 3-week pilot to validate latency and burn rate, maybe hosted initially then move to dedicated if numbers fit.
[03:24] Alexi: that's common. Our recommended flow: 1) hosted pilot with debug metrics and KV caching enabled, 2) 3-week benchmark with your traces, 3) if steady-state economics are favorable, we propose a dedicated pool with a 3-6 month commit.
[03:38] Priya: procurement question — how does invoicing and SLAs differ for dedicated vs hosted? we have to route through finance.
[03:45] Alexi: hosted is pay-as-you-go with monthly invoicing, standard SLA. Dedicated is contract with reserved monthly fee + lower variable. We can hand off standard SOW and legal terms; we'll flag enterprise terms early.
[03:57] Priya: ok please include a sample SOW and SOC2 evidence in the package.
[04:02] Alexi: yes — security doc link we'll share.
[04:06] [04:06] Mateo: i want to understand worst-case burn during spikes — we do promos where QPS jumps 6x for hours. what's the fallback pattern?
[04:14] Samir: we can do burst capacity on dedicated (short-term GPUs) or auto-fallback routing to a lower-cost compatible model in hosted that keeps latency but may change quality. Fallback costs depend on the model used. We can simulate.
[04:28] Leah: what about region residency when bursting? we can't have data leave region.
[04:33] Jules: that's a key constraint — we can provision burst in the same region for Dedicated; for hosted, region coverage depends on availability. We'll note that in the pilot config.
[04:44] Alexi: i'd like to run a simple worked example now to show sensitivity. If you keep 2M tokens and have 25k budget, that gives roughly $0.0125 per token? sorry math slip — let me do the math out loud. 25,000 / 2,000,000 = $0.0125 per token — wait that's per token in dollars, but our earlier per-token numbers were per-thousand?
[05:05] Mateo: i think youre mixing token vs 1k tokens. we usually quote per 1k tokens; clarify the unit.
[05:10] Alexi: thanks — correct. Our hosted numbers were per 1k tokens: hosted $0.8-$1.2 per 1k tokens; dedicated amortized $0.45-$0.7 per 1k. With 2M tokens that's 2,000 units of 1k so budget 25k / 2,000 = $12.50 per 1k — oh that's way higher, which is good — ive made a mistake in decimal.
[05:34] Leah: yes that makes more sense — so your numbers look well under our cap, but we need to account for peak-strike inefficiencies and infra overhead.
[05:41] Samir: exactly. For spikes, effective per-1k token cost can double if you have idle capacity or underutilized reserved GPUs. That's why we model utilization and have a burst plan.
[05:51] Mateo: can you model three scenarios? low, expected, high utilization with costs?
[05:55] Alexi: we will — action item. We'll send a spreadsheet: hosted baseline, dedicated steady-state, dedicated + burst, and sensitivity to cache hit rate.
[06:05] Priya: procurement will need vendor references and standard insurance language.
[06:09] Alexi: we'll include references and our insurance certs.
[06:12] [06:12] Leah: on privacy, we need audit logs per token and redaction hooks. Is that supported?
[06:18] Jules: yes, per-request tracing and audit logs available; redaction is a preprocessor we can help wire with our SDK. Also we support bringing your KMS for Dedicated/Private.
[06:27] Mateo: about private — you mentioned an on-prem private option earlier; what are the rough cost and time differences vs dedicated?
[06:34] Samir: private on-prem typically has a larger up-front integration effort and a minimum license; OPEX for hardware + ops is higher but gives maximal data control. Time-to-live is usually 8-12 weeks for first deploy vs 2-3 weeks for hosted pilot and 4-6 weeks for dedicated provisioning.
[06:53] Leah: that's in line with expectations. Our immediate priority is to prove P95 latency and cost fit; residency is second but critical for full production.
[07:02] Alexi: for the pilot we recommend enabling KV cache, medium quantization (q4) for a staged quality test, and a throughput run with a 30k request trace to measure P95.
[07:13] Mateo: can you do that test with our sample prompts?
[07:16] Samir: yes, if you supply the traces we'll run it in our hosted infra under telemetry and share the token-level breakdown.
[07:23] Leah: one more question on support: during pilot do we get an SE dedicated to troubleshoot?
[07:28] Alexi: yes — samir and jules will be the points. We'll include 8 hours/week triage for pilot.
[07:34] Priya: ok, timeline wise, if we sign off on pilot by 2026-10-20, can you start the hosted pilot the next week?
[07:41] Alexi: yes, target start 2026-10-26 is feasible. We'll need PO or approval, and the traces.
[07:47] [07:47] Mateo: pricing — will you include a small exploratory credit? we've seen credits help close pilots.
[07:52] Alexi: we can include a one-time credit for pilot to offset early burn, subject to standard pilot terms. We'll include that in the package.
[07:59] Leah: great. i also want the test to include a worst-case 6x spike run and a fallback to cheaper model to see latency and quality change.
[08:09] Samir: can do — we'll show a fallback matrix with quality delta and cost delta.
[08:13] Alexi: ok wrapping up, quick recap: we'll send pricing scenarios and pilot SOW, you will share prompt traces, procurement will confirm PO path, and schedule a benchmark run week of Oct 19/26 depending on approvals.
[08:26] Priya: noted.
[08:29] Leah: thanks all, this was helpful.
[08:32] Alexi: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts.

Notes/Imperfect transcription markers: sometimes 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cash', 'quant' as 'kwant', minor speaker misattribution possible.

End of call.
